# CAICT: 算力电力协同发展研究报告 (2025)

China Academy of Information and Communications Technology, Cloud Computing & Big Data Institute. Published May 2025.

## Key Findings (recovered via Exa PDF fetch)

### Data Center Electricity Consumption
- 2023: National data center electricity consumption = **150 billion kWh (150 TWh)**, up 15.4% YoY.
- Same period, total national electricity consumption grew 5.8%.
- 2023: Data center electricity = **1.6% of total national electricity consumption**.
- Historical data center electricity (billion kWh): 2019: 824, 2020: 939, 2021: 1,116, 2022: 1,300, 2023: 1,500.

### 2030 Projections (3 scenarios)
- **High scenario** (AI explosive growth): >700 billion kWh by 2030, **5.3%** of national electricity.
- **Medium scenario** (AI steady growth): >400 billion kWh by 2030, **3.0%** of national electricity.
- **Low scenario** (AI slow growth): ~300 billion kWh by 2030, **2.3%** of national electricity.

### AI as Growth Driver
- OpenAI GPT-3 training consumed 1.287 million kWh (per Stanford AI Index 2023).
- GPT-4 parameter doubling significantly increases energy consumption.
- IDC: 35% of Chinese enterprises doing initial LLM testing/POC; 24% heavily invested in GenAI.
- By 2025, >50% of China Top 500 enterprises will use AI/automation for data detection and processing.
- China intelligent computing scale expected to grow **33.9% annually** from 2022 to 2027 (IDC).

### Green Power Requirements
- Dec 2023: NDRC et al. "Eastern Data, Western Computing" implementation opinion — first mention of "computing-power synergy"; target: **new data centers at national hub nodes >80% green power by end 2025**.
- Jul 2024: "Data Center Green Low-Carbon Development Special Action Plan" — target: initial two-way computing-power mechanism by end 2025.
- Jul 2024: "New Power System Action Plan (2024-2027)" — integrate source-load-storage resources, improve data center green power share.

### Challenges
- Computing demand and electricity use clustering puts pressure on local grids.
- High-standard power supply needs vs low-load operation imbalance.
- Green power supply-demand gap; difficulties in green power trading.
- Green power direct supply needs acceleration; source-grid-load-storage development insufficient.

### Six Key Measures
1. Source-load interaction for power balance and low-carbon transition
2. Storage-load interaction to unlock data center grid feedback potential
3. Grid-load coordination for safe/reliable supply
4. Source-grid-load-storage integration for deep computing-power fusion
5. Computing load scheduling for precise spatiotemporal supply-demand matching
6. Green power/green certificate trading to improve data center green power use
